name: ZITLAS Odia Dalma Bowl
description: An Odisha-style dal cooked with mixed vegetables and a light panch phoron tempering — a distinct regional dal-vegetable combination not resembling any other dal dish in the database.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables (pumpkin, raw banana, papaya) — 70 g
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with mixed vegetables and turmeric for 3 whistles until soft.
Mash lightly.
Heat oil, temper panch phoron, and pour over the dal.
Simmer 3-4 minutes and serve hot.
why_it_works: Panch phoron tempering and the specific vegetable mix (pumpkin, raw banana) give this a genuinely distinct Odia flavour from any Punjabi or South Indian dal in the database
One-pot, mostly hands-off
Traditionally a lunch dish, reframed here as a hearty breakfast bowl

name: ZITLAS Kashmiri Nadru Yakhni Bowl
description: Lotus stem (nadru) simmered in a mild yogurt-based Kashmiri gravy — introducing lotus stem, a vegetable not used anywhere else in the database.
ingredients: Fennel powder, ginger powder, cardamom — 5 g
instructions: Shallow-fry the sliced lotus stem in oil until lightly browned; set aside.
Whisk curd with fennel powder, ginger powder and cardamom.
Heat the whisked curd gently in a pan, stirring continuously to prevent curdling, until it thickens slightly.
Add the fried lotus stem and simmer 5-6 minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Lotus stem is a genuinely unique vegetable for the database, with a distinct crunchy-then-tender texture
Kashmiri yakhni technique (yogurt-based, no onion-garlic) is a distinct regional gravy style
Curd base supplies real protein

name: ZITLAS Himachali Siddu
description: A steamed, stuffed whole wheat bread from Himachal Pradesh, filled with a spiced walnut-poppy seed paste — a distinct steamed-bread format not resembling any dhokla, idli or momo in the database.
instructions: Knead atta with yeast and warm water into a soft dough; let it rise for about 1.5 hours until doubled.
Mix crushed walnuts with cumin seeds and a little oil for the filling.
Divide the dough, flatten each portion, add filling, and seal into a ball.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 18-20 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with a drizzle of ghee or chutney.
why_it_works: Yeasted, steamed bread technique is entirely different from any dhokla, idli, khaman or momo already in the database
Walnut filling introduces a nut rarely used as a main filling elsewhere
Himachal Pradesh regional cuisine represented for the first time

name: ZITLAS Chhattisgarhi Bore Basi
description: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water and served with curd and green chilli the next morning — a traditional fermented-rice breakfast distinct from any curd rice or poha dish in the database.
instructions: Soak cooked rice in water overnight at room temperature (this begins a mild natural fermentation).
In the morning, drain most of the water, leaving the rice slightly moist.
Mix in curd, chopped green chilli, onion and salt.
Eat at room temperature.
Note: overnight soak folded into prep time above.
why_it_works: Mild overnight fermentation gives bore basi a distinct tang and gut-friendly quality that plain curd rice doesn't have
Traditional Chhattisgarhi farmer's breakfast, genuinely different preparation from any other rice dish in the database
Very low cost, zero cooking in the morning

name: ZITLAS Litti-Style Baked Sattu Balls
description: Whole wheat dough balls stuffed with spiced sattu and baked until crisp — the traditional Bihar-Jharkhand litti, made oven-baked instead of over open coals.
ingredients: Ajwain, nigella seeds, pickle masala — 6 g
instructions: Mix sattu with mustard oil, ajwain, nigella seeds and pickle masala, adding a little water to form a moist, crumbly filling.
Knead atta into a firm dough and divide into balls; flatten each, stuff with the sattu filling and seal into a tight ball.
Bake at 200°C for 22-25 minutes, turning occasionally, until the crust is browned and firm.
Serve with a drizzle of ghee and a side of chokha or curd.
why_it_works: Litti's stuffed-and-baked ball technique is distinct from the flat stuffed parathas already using sattu in the database
Baking is a genuine practical adaptation of the traditional coal-roasted method for a home kitchen
High protein, very low cost

name: ZITLAS Jhangora Millet Upma
description: Upma made with jhangora (barnyard millet), a grain traditionally used in Uttarakhand and during fasting — a genuinely new millet base for the database.
instructions: Rinse jhangora well.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute vegetables 3 minutes.
Add jhangora and water (1:2.5 ratio), cover and simmer 10-12 minutes until soft.
Fluff and serve hot.
why_it_works: Jhangora is a genuinely uncommon millet outside Uttarakhand and fasting-day cooking
Very easy to digest, traditionally used for the same reason
Same familiar upma technique, new grain

name: ZITLAS Black Rice Porridge
description: A warm porridge made from black rice (chak-hao), a Manipuri specialty grain with a naturally nutty flavour and deep purple colour — a genuinely different rice variety from any other rice dish in the database.
instructions: Soak black rice for at least 2 hours (it takes longer to cook than white rice).
Pressure cook the soaked rice with water for 4-5 whistles until very soft and porridge-like.
Stir in jaggery and coconut milk.
Simmer 2-3 minutes and serve warm.
Note: soak time folded into prep above.
why_it_works: Black rice is a genuinely distinct grain variety, naturally higher in antioxidants than white or brown rice
Manipuri regional specialty rarely represented in fitness recipe collections
Distinctive colour and nutty flavour unlike any other porridge in the database

name: ZITLAS Bamboo Shoot Vegetable Bowl
description: Fermented bamboo shoot stir-fried with vegetables, a staple ingredient across several Northeast Indian states — introducing an ingredient not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and dried red chilli briefly.
Add bamboo shoot and vegetables, stir-frying for 6-8 minutes until softened.
Season lightly (fermented bamboo shoot is already quite flavourful) and serve hot.
why_it_works: Fermented bamboo shoot is a genuinely unique ingredient for the database, common across Northeast Indian states but rarely seen in mainstream fitness recipe collections
Fermentation itself adds gut-friendly qualities
Distinct sharp, tangy flavour profile unlike anything else in the database

name: ZITLAS Assamese Fish and Rice Bowl
description: A very light, minimally spiced Assamese-style fish preparation with tomato and mustard oil, served over rice — a distinct regional fish technique from the Bengali, Kerala or Chettinad versions already in the database.
instructions: Rub the fish with turmeric and a little salt.
Heat mustard oil, add tomato and cook until it breaks down into a thin, tangy gravy.
Add the fish and whole green chilli, and simmer gently for 6-8 minutes until just cooked, without heavy spicing.
Serve over warm rice.
why_it_works: Assamese cooking is known for minimal spicing and reliance on mustard oil and souring agents like tomato, a genuinely distinct technique from the richer Bengali or Chettinad fish preparations already in the database
Very light, easy to digest
Fourth distinct regional fish preparation, broadening variety further

name: ZITLAS Fermented Greens Soup Bowl
description: A warm soup made from fermented leafy greens, inspired by Sikkim's gundruk — a fermented-vegetable soup format not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and dried red chilli.
Add tomato and cook until soft.
Add fermented greens and water, and simmer 10-12 minutes into a tangy, warming soup.
Serve hot in a bowl.
why_it_works: Fermented greens give this soup a distinct sour, umami depth unlike any other soup in the database
Sikkim and hill-region cooking rarely represented in fitness recipe collections
Warm, comforting for cold mornings

name: ZITLAS Office Lunchbox Rajma Rice Bowl
description: Rajma and rice specifically portioned and packed to travel well for a few hours without refrigeration — designed around the constraint of an office lunchbox, not just a home meal.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and garam masala.
Add boiled rajma and cook down until the gravy is thick and clingy rather than watery (this is what makes it travel well).
Pack the thick rajma over rice in a lunchbox while still warm — sealing it warm helps it stay fresher longer.
Eat within 3-4 hours, reheating if a microwave is available.
why_it_works: Deliberately thickened gravy (not the usual thinner home-style rajma) specifically so it travels without leaking or spoiling as fast
Designed around the actual constraint of a few hours outside a fridge, not just home eating
High protein, filling for a work morning

name: ZITLAS Office Lunchbox Chole Wrap
description: A thick, dry-cooked chole filling wrapped in roti specifically designed to hold together and stay fresh for an office commute, unlike a wetter chole-bhature preparation.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and chole masala.
Add boiled chana and cook down, mashing a few lightly, until thick and dry rather than saucy.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly.
Wrap in foil — it holds together well for several hours.
why_it_works: Deliberately dry-cooked chole (unlike a typical wet chole curry) so it doesn't make the wrap soggy over a few hours
Designed specifically for the lunchbox use case rather than immediate home eating
High protein and fiber for sustained energy through a work morning

name: ZITLAS Post-Workout Banana Peanut Protein Shake
description: A fast-absorbing banana and peanut butter shake specifically timed for right after a workout — a thinner, quicker-to-drink format than a smoothie bowl, meant to be consumed within the post-workout window.
instructions: Blend banana, peanut butter and milk together until completely smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink within 30-45 minutes of finishing your workout.
No need to chew or wait — this is meant to be consumed quickly.
why_it_works: Explicitly timed for the post-workout recovery window rather than being a general-purpose breakfast
Thin, fast-drinking format gets nutrients in quickly, unlike a spoon-eaten smoothie bowl
Banana replenishes glycogen while milk and peanut butter provide protein

name: ZITLAS Post-Workout Chocolate Banana Milk
description: A simple cocoa-banana-milk recovery drink — a different flavour direction from the peanut butter shake, for users who prefer a chocolate option after training.
instructions: Blend banana, milk and cocoa powder together until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink soon after training.
Chill briefly if a cold drink is preferred after a hot workout.
why_it_works: Chocolate flavour gives users a genuine choice alongside the peanut butter version in this batch, without added sugar since banana provides the sweetness
Same fast-absorbing, post-workout-timed format
Simple three-ingredient recovery drink

name: ZITLAS Overnight Fruit and Nut Muesli
description: Muesli soaked overnight in milk with chopped fruit mixed in — a longer-soak, softer-texture variant distinct from the No-Cook Muesli Bowl eaten immediately.
instructions: Combine muesli, milk and chopped apple in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Stir and eat cold in the morning — the texture is noticeably softer than muesli eaten immediately.
Note: overnight soak folded into prep time above.
why_it_works: Overnight soaking gives a completely different, softer texture from the crunchy immediate-eat muesli bowl in Batch 7
Apple adds fresh fruit and fiber not in the plain version
Genuinely zero morning effort

name: ZITLAS Watermelon Paneer Salad Bowl
description: Cubed watermelon and paneer tossed together with mint — an unusual sweet-savoury fruit-and-dairy pairing, distinct from any other paneer or fruit recipe in the database.
instructions: Cube the watermelon and paneer to similar sizes.
Toss together with chopped mint and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: Watermelon is a genuinely new fruit for the database, and pairing it with paneer is an unusual but refreshing sweet-savoury combination
Entirely no-cook, very light and hydrating
Good hot-weather breakfast option

name: ZITLAS Mango Lassi Protein Bowl
description: A thick, spoonable mango lassi made with Greek yogurt instead of regular curd — a protein-boosted, bowl-format take on the classic drink, distinct from a thin sippable lassi.
instructions: Blend mango, Greek yogurt and cardamom powder together until thick and smooth (use less liquid than a drinkable lassi).
Pour into a bowl — it should be thick enough to eat with a spoon.
Eat immediately while chilled.
why_it_works: Greek yogurt gives meaningfully more protein than the regular curd used in a traditional lassi
Bowl format (eaten with a spoon) is distinct from a drinkable glass of lassi
Seasonal mango makes this a genuinely different fruit base from any other recipe in the database

name: ZITLAS Papaya and Curd Breakfast Bowl
description: Chopped ripe papaya folded into curd with a touch of honey — introducing papaya, a fruit not used anywhere else in the database, known for being easy on digestion.
instructions: Chop the papaya into small cubes.
Fold into curd.
Drizzle with honey.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Papaya is a genuinely new fruit for the database, commonly recommended for easy digestion
Very low cost and widely available
Entirely no-cook, light breakfast

name: ZITLAS Guava and Peanut Chaat Bowl
description: Chopped guava tossed with roasted peanuts and chaat masala — introducing guava, a fruit not used anywhere else in the database, paired with a crunchy protein element.
instructions: Chop the guava into bite-sized pieces.
Toss with crushed peanuts, chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Guava is high in fiber and vitamin C, and is a genuinely new fruit for the database
Peanuts add crunch and protein a plain fruit chaat would lack
Entirely no-cook, high fiber

name: ZITLAS Apple Cinnamon Oats Bowl
description: Grated apple cooked briefly with oats and cinnamon — a warm, naturally sweet oats preparation distinct from the banana, date or peanut butter versions already in the database.
instructions: Heat milk in a pan, add oats and grated apple.
Simmer 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until the oats soften and thicken.
Stir in cinnamon powder and serve warm.
why_it_works: Apple and cinnamon give a genuinely different flavour direction from the banana, date or peanut butter oats already in the database
Naturally sweetened, no added sugar needed
Warm, comforting for cooler mornings

name: ZITLAS Pineapple Paneer Skewers
description: Grilled paneer and pineapple chunks on skewers — a sweet-savoury grilled combination distinct from the plain Paneer Tikka Skewers already in the database.
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in curd and tikka masala for at least 15 minutes.
Thread paneer and pineapple alternately onto skewers.
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Pineapple's natural sweetness against savoury marinated paneer is a genuinely different flavour combination from the plain vegetable tikka skewers already in the database
Grilled, not fried — low added oil
Fun, distinct presentation

name: ZITLAS Mixed Berries and Greek Yogurt Bowl
description: Greek yogurt topped with mixed berries — introducing berries as a fruit category not used anywhere else in the database, paired with a high-protein dairy base.
instructions: Spoon Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Top with mixed berries.
Drizzle honey over the top.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Berries are a genuinely new fruit category for the database, distinct from banana, mango, apple or citrus
High protein from Greek yogurt makes this more filling than a typical fruit bowl
Entirely no-cook, premium but simple

name: ZITLAS Roasted Beetroot Hummus Toast
description: A homemade hummus made from chickpeas and roasted beetroot, spread on toast — a Middle-Eastern-inspired spread adapted with an Indian pulse base and a distinct pink colour.
instructions: Roast the beetroot in an oven at 200°C for about 20 minutes until soft, or use pre-roasted.
Blend boiled chana with the roasted beetroot, garlic, lemon juice and oil into a smooth hummus.
Toast the bread.
Spread the beetroot hummus generously over the toast.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: A ZITLAS-inspired adaptation of hummus using chana rather than imported chickpea brands, with beetroot giving it a distinct colour and earthy sweetness
Genuinely different spread from every chutney or thecha used elsewhere in the database
Batch-makeable and keeps for a few days refrigerated

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Moong Hummus Toast
description: A hummus-style spread made from sprouted moong instead of chickpeas — a lighter, greener variant from the beetroot chana hummus in this batch.
ingredients: Garlic, lemon juice, cumin powder — 6 g
instructions: Blend moong sprouts with garlic, lemon juice, cumin powder and oil into a smooth, spreadable paste.
Toast the bread.
Spread the moong hummus generously over the toast.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Sprouted moong gives a lighter, greener hummus with a genuinely different base pulse from the chana version in this batch
No cooking needed at all since sprouts are already tender
Cheaper and quicker than the roasted-beetroot version

name: ZITLAS Zucchini Besan Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with grated zucchini mixed in — introducing zucchini, a vegetable not used anywhere else in the database, in a familiar chilla format.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, cumin seeds and ajwain into a batter.
Mix in grated zucchini (its moisture helps thin the batter naturally).
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Zucchini is a genuinely new vegetable for the database, with a mild flavour and high water content
Same reliable chilla technique, different vegetable each time keeps the rotation varied
Very low calorie filling

name: ZITLAS Broccoli Paneer Salad Bowl
description: A no-cook salad of lightly blanched broccoli and cubed paneer tossed with lemon — introducing broccoli, a vegetable not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Toss with cubed paneer, lemon juice and black pepper.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.
why_it_works: Broccoli is a genuinely new vegetable for the database, offering a different fiber and micronutrient profile from cauliflower or cabbage
Very quick blanching, mostly a cold assembly
High protein, low calorie combination

name: ZITLAS Mushroom Besan Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with finely chopped mushrooms mixed in — introducing mushroom, an umami-rich ingredient not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Saute the chopped mushrooms briefly in a dry pan to release excess moisture, then cool.
Whisk besan with water, black pepper and cumin seeds into a batter, and mix in the sauteed mushrooms.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Mushroom's natural umami is a genuinely different flavour direction from any vegetable chilla already in the database
Pre-sauteing the mushroom prevents a soggy batter
New ingredient broadens the vegetable range

name: ZITLAS Mushroom Egg Scramble Toast
description: Scrambled egg with sauteed mushrooms served over toast — combining two umami-forward ingredients in a single dish, distinct from a plain egg bhurji.
instructions: Heat oil, saute sliced mushrooms until they release their moisture and brown slightly, about 4-5 minutes.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling gently with the mushrooms until just set.
Toast the bread and spoon the mushroom-egg scramble over the top.
Season with black pepper and serve.
why_it_works: Mushroom's savoury depth pairs distinctly with egg, different from any tomato-onion-based egg preparation elsewhere in the database
Two umami ingredients combined intentionally
Quick, familiar toast format

name: ZITLAS Quinoa Stuffed Capsicum
description: Capsicum halves stuffed with cooked quinoa and vegetables, then baked — a distinct grain-stuffed-vegetable format from the paneer bhurji stuffed capsicum already in the database.
instructions: Saute onion and tomato in oil until soft, then mix with cooked quinoa, cumin powder and black pepper.
Stuff the mixture into the capsicum halves.
Bake at 190°C for 18-20 minutes until the capsicum softens.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Quinoa filling is a genuinely different stuffing from the paneer bhurji version already in the database — grain-based rather than dairy-based
Baked rather than steamed, giving the capsicum a slightly different texture
Complete protein grain in a distinctive presentation

name: ZITLAS Baked Stuffed Tomato with Egg
description: A large tomato hollowed out and baked with an egg cracked inside — a distinct vegetable-as-vessel format using tomato rather than capsicum.
instructions: Slice the top off the tomato and hollow out the pulp and seeds, leaving a sturdy shell.
Crack the egg into the hollowed tomato.
Season with black pepper and oregano.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until the egg is set and the tomato has softened.
Serve warm, eaten straight from the tomato shell.
why_it_works: Using a tomato rather than capsicum as the vessel gives a distinctly juicier, tangier result
Novel presentation — the egg bakes directly inside the fruit
Low added fat since no oil is needed

name: ZITLAS Spinach Corn Sandwich
description: A grilled sandwich filled with sauteed spinach and sweet corn — a distinct vegetable pairing from any other sandwich in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute spinach until wilted, then mix in boiled corn and black pepper.
Spread the mixture between two bread slices.
Grill on a lightly oiled tawa until both sides are golden and crisp.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Spinach and corn together is a genuinely different pairing from every other sandwich filling in the database
Iron from spinach and natural sweetness from corn balance well
Quick, familiar grilled-sandwich format

name: ZITLAS Beetroot Hummus Wrap
description: The roasted beetroot hummus from this batch rolled inside a roti with fresh vegetables — a wrap format for the same spread, distinct from eating it on toast.
instructions: Blend boiled chana with roasted beetroot and a little oil into a smooth hummus.
Roll out and roast the atta into a roti.
Spread the beetroot hummus onto the roti, add cucumber slices, and roll tightly.
Serve immediately or wrap for later.
why_it_works: Wrap format is a genuinely different eating experience from the toast version in this batch, and travels better
Same hummus base, different delivery vehicle
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Roasted Vegetable Quinoa Bowl
description: Oven-roasted mixed vegetables tossed with cooked quinoa — a distinct roasted-vegetable technique from the boiled or sauteed vegetable preparations used elsewhere with quinoa.
instructions: Toss chopped vegetables with oil, black pepper and oregano.
Roast at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until edges are lightly charred.
Toss the roasted vegetables with cooked quinoa.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Roasting concentrates the vegetables' flavour differently from boiling or steaming, a genuinely different technique from the plain Quinoa Vegetable Poha-Style Bowl already in the database
Complete protein grain base
Good make-ahead-and-reheat option

name: ZITLAS Sweet Buckwheat Porridge with Nuts
description: Buckwheat (kuttu) flour cooked into a sweet milk porridge with walnuts — a dessert-style preparation distinct from the savoury kuttu pancake and chilla already in the database.
instructions: Whisk kuttu flour into a little cold milk to avoid lumps.
Heat the rest of the milk, add the flour mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened.
Stir in jaggery, top with crushed walnuts, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Sweet, milk-based preparation gives kuttu a genuinely different everyday use from its savoury pancake or chilla forms already in the database
Walnuts add healthy fat and crunch
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Puffed Amaranth Ladoo
description: No-bake ladoo made from puffed amaranth (rajgira) bound with jaggery — a popular fasting-day sweet reframed as a portable breakfast bite, distinct from the flour-based rajgira porridge already in the database.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a kadai on low heat until it forms a thick syrup.
Turn off heat, quickly mix in puffed amaranth, coating evenly.
Shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Puffed form gives a light, crisp texture entirely different from the smooth flour-based rajgira porridge already in the database
Traditional fasting-day sweet, genuinely portable
Batch-made once for the week

name: ZITLAS Til Gud Ladoo
description: No-bake sesame seed and jaggery ladoo — a traditional winter sweet using sesame (til) as the primary ingredient, a seed not used as a main component anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Dry-roast the sesame seeds in a kadai on low heat until fragrant and lightly golden, about 4-5 minutes.
Melt jaggery with ghee separately until it forms a thick syrup.
Mix the roasted sesame seeds into the jaggery syrup, coating evenly.
Shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Cool completely and store for up to two weeks.
why_it_works: Sesame seeds are used as the primary ingredient here rather than a minor tempering element, a genuinely new role for them in the database
Traditional winter combination believed to provide warmth and energy
High in calcium and healthy fats

name: ZITLAS Walnut Date No-Cook Bites
description: No-cook energy bites made from blended walnuts and dates — a raw, unheated preparation distinct from every cooked ladoo or chikki in the database.
instructions: Blend walnuts and dates together in a mixer until they form a sticky, dough-like mixture (add cocoa powder if using).
Shape into 8 small balls with your hands.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week.
why_it_works: Entirely no-cook, unlike every jaggery-based ladoo or chikki elsewhere in the database which require heating
Walnuts bring omega-3 fats not present in the peanut- or sesame-based bites
Raw preparation keeps more of the nuts' natural nutrients intact

name: ZITLAS Makhana Kheer Protein Bowl
description: A warm, milk-based makhana kheer with a portion-controlled serving size — a dessert-style, warm preparation distinct from the yogurt parfait, dry trail mix or savoury chaat uses of makhana already in the database.
instructions: Lightly crush the makhana.
Heat milk in a pan, add the crushed makhana and simmer 8-10 minutes until softened and the milk thickens slightly.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder.
Simmer 2 more minutes and serve warm.
why_it_works: Warm, milk-simmered kheer format is the fourth distinct makhana preparation in the database, alongside the yogurt parfait, dry trail mix and savoury chaat
Single-serving format keeps portions controlled for a dessert-style breakfast
Traditional festive dish reframed as a controlled everyday option

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Dates
description: Pitted dates stuffed with a small amount of spiced paneer — a bite-sized sweet-savoury combination not resembling any other paneer or date recipe in the database.
instructions: Mash paneer with a pinch of cardamom powder.
Slit each pitted date lengthwise and stuff with a small amount of the paneer mixture.
Eat as bite-sized pieces, 3-4 at a time.
why_it_works: Bite-sized, stuffed-fruit format is genuinely different from any other paneer preparation in the database, which are all savoury mains
No cooking involved
Natural sweetness from dates balances the mild paneer filling

name: ZITLAS Egg White Spinach Scramble Bowl
description: A spinach-forward egg white scramble served as a bowl rather than a wrap — distinct from the Egg White Veggie Wrap already in the database by both format and the vegetable ratio.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until soft, then add spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the egg whites and scramble gently until just set, mixing through the spinach.
Season with black pepper and serve in a bowl, no bread or wrap.
why_it_works: Spinach makes up the bulk of this dish rather than being a minor addition, and the bowl format (no bread) is genuinely different from the existing wrap version
Very low fat, high protein
Good for a lean cutting-phase breakfast

name: ZITLAS Overnight Mango Oats
description: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk with pureed mango — a seasonal fruit variant of overnight oats distinct from the banana, date or chia versions already in the database.
instructions: Combine oats, milk and pureed mango in a jar.
Stir well.
Refrigerate overnight.
Stir again and eat cold in the morning.
Note: overnight soak folded into prep time above.
why_it_works: Mango puree gives a genuinely different, seasonal flavour direction from the banana, date or chia-based overnight oats already in the database
Zero morning prep once made the night before
Naturally sweet, no added sugar needed

name: ZITLAS Besan Pancake Stack with Curd
description: Small savoury besan pancakes stacked and topped with curd — a griddle-pancake format for besan, distinct from a chilla by being smaller, thicker, and stacked rather than one large round.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, cumin seeds and ajwain into a thick, pourable batter.
Cook small, thick pancakes (about palm-sized) on a lightly oiled tawa, 2 minutes per side.
Stack 3-4 small pancakes.
Top with a dollop of curd and serve.
why_it_works: Small, thick, stacked pancake format is a genuinely different construction from a single large thin chilla
Curd topping (not a side) makes this distinct from every other besan preparation in the database
Fun, different presentation of a familiar batter

name: ZITLAS Sweet Ragi Pancake with Jaggery Syrup
description: A sweet, griddle-cooked ragi pancake served with a thin jaggery syrup — a dessert-style ragi preparation distinct from the savoury ragi dosa or idli already in the database.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour with milk into a smooth, pourable batter.
Melt half the jaggery in a little water to make a thin syrup; set aside.
Cook small pancakes on a lightly oiled tawa, 2 minutes per side.
Drizzle with the jaggery syrup before serving.
why_it_works: Sweet pancake format gives ragi a genuinely different everyday use from the savoury dosa or idli versions already in the database
Jaggery syrup instead of refined sugar
Calcium-rich grain in a dessert-style presentation

name: ZITLAS Sweet Foxtail Millet Porridge with Dates
description: Foxtail millet cooked into a sweet milk porridge with chopped dates — a dessert-style preparation distinct from the savoury foxtail millet upma and pongal already in the database.
instructions: Rinse the foxtail millet.
Simmer in milk for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and the milk thickens.
Stir in chopped dates and cardamom powder, simmer 2 more minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Sweet, milk-based preparation gives foxtail millet a third distinct role in the database, alongside its savoury upma and pongal forms
Naturally sweetened by dates
Warm, comforting texture

name: ZITLAS Lauki Halwa Protein Bowl
description: A portion-controlled bottle gourd (lauki) halwa made with less ghee than the traditional version, served in a small single-serving bowl — a vegetable-based dessert-breakfast paralleling the Moong Dal Halwa already in the database.
instructions: Squeeze excess water from the grated lauki.
Heat ghee in a kadai, add the lauki and saute for 5 minutes until it softens.
Add milk and simmer until it reduces and thickens, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in jaggery and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve warm in a small bowl.
why_it_works: Vegetable-based dessert (lauki, not a grain or dal) gives a genuinely different base from the Moong Dal Halwa already in the database
Deliberately less ghee than a traditional halwa, and a single-serving portion to control intake
Low calorie for a dessert-style dish thanks to lauki's high water content

name: ZITLAS Gajar Halwa Protein Bowl
description: A portion-controlled carrot (gajar) halwa made with less ghee and a portion of milk powder for extra protein — a second vegetable-based dessert-breakfast, distinct from the lauki version by using carrot's natural sweetness and colour.
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai, add grated carrot and saute for 5 minutes.
Add milk and simmer until it reduces significantly, about 10-12 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in milk powder for extra protein and creaminess, cooking 2-3 more minutes.
Serve warm in a small bowl.
why_it_works: Milk powder addition gives this notably more protein than a traditional gajar halwa, a distinct nutritional strategy from the lauki version in this batch
Carrot's natural sweetness needs no added jaggery or sugar
Portion-controlled to keep this a reasonable breakfast rather than a heavy dessert serving

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Baked Sweet Potato
description: A baked sweet potato split and stuffed with spiced paneer bhurji — a distinct filling from the curd-topped or chaat versions of sweet potato already in the database.
instructions: Bake the whole sweet potato at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile, heat oil, saute onion, add turmeric and chilli powder, then paneer, cooking 3-4 minutes.
Split the baked sweet potato open and stuff generously with the paneer mixture.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Paneer filling gives notably more protein than the curd-topped or chaat-style sweet potato preparations already in the database
Filling makes this a more complete meal rather than a side
Baked base keeps this simple and mostly hands-off

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chickpea and Pumpkin Seed Trail Mix
description: A dry mix of roasted chickpeas and pumpkin seeds — introducing pumpkin seeds, a genuinely new seed for the database, in a portable no-cook format.
instructions: Combine roasted chana and pumpkin seeds in a small container.
Mix well.
Carry and eat on the move, or as a sit-down bowl.
why_it_works: Pumpkin seeds are unusually high in protein and zinc and haven't been used anywhere else in the database
Entirely dry, shelf-stable mix
Genuinely no prep beyond mixing

name: ZITLAS Flax and Chia Energy Bites
description: No-bake bites combining ground flaxseed and chia seeds bound with dates — a double-seed combination distinct from the single-seed flaxseed-peanut bites already in the database.
instructions: Blend the dates in a mixer until they form a sticky paste (or mash by hand).
Mix in ground flaxseed and chia seeds until well combined into a firm, moist mixture.
Shape into 8 small balls.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week.
why_it_works: Combining two seeds (flax and chia) rather than one gives a broader omega-3 and fiber profile than the single-seed bites elsewhere in the database
Entirely no-cook, unlike the jaggery-syrup ladoo bites
Genuinely portable

name: ZITLAS Coconut Water Chia Pudding
description: Chia seeds soaked in coconut water instead of milk — a dairy-free, lighter chia pudding distinct from the milk or soya-milk versions already in the database.
instructions: Stir chia seeds into coconut water, whisking well to prevent clumping.
Add honey and stir again.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until thickened.
Eat cold with a spoon.
why_it_works: Coconut water base is a genuinely different, dairy-free liquid from the milk or soya-milk chia puddings already in the database
Naturally hydrating and light, good for hot mornings
Fully vegan and low calorie
